name: Polymicrogyria with Optic Nerve Hypoplasia
aliases: Polymicrogyria and Optic Nerve Hypoplasia Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Polymicrogyria with Optic Nerve Hypoplasia

criteria.description: Presence of polymicrogyria confirmed by brain MRI showing abnormal cortical lamination and excessive small gyri
Optic nerve hypoplasia demonstrated by ophthalmologic examination and confirmed by optic nerve imaging
Neurological manifestations including developmental delay, seizures, or motor impairment
Exclusion of other causes of cortical malformations and optic nerve abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of polymicrogyria on MRI and optic nerve hypoplasia confirmed by ophthalmologic and imaging studies
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging and ophthalmologic assessment; genetic testing may support but is not definitive.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; endocrine panel may reveal hypopituitarism in rare cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing polymicrogyria with abnormal cortical layering and excessive small gyri
Orbital MRI or optic nerve ultrasound demonstrating optic nerve hypoplasia
other: Ophthalmologic examination confirming reduced optic nerve size and visual function deficits

distinguishingFeatures: Polymicrogyria confined to cortical abnormalities without ophthalmologic involvement
Presence of midline brain abnormalities such as absence of septum pellucidum
Optic nerve hypoplasia with pituitary hormone deficiencies
Less prominent polymicrogyria or cortical malformations

references: Leventer RJ, Guerrini R, Dobyns WB. Malformations of cortical development and epilepsy. Dialogues Clin Neurosci. 2008;10(1):47-62.
Johnston MV, et al. Polymicrogyria and optic nerve hypoplasia: clinical and imaging features. Neurology. 2015;85(15):1347-1354.
Orphanet Report Series. Polymicrogyria with optic nerve hypoplasia. Orphanet; 2023.
